title: Parish and Inheritance
premise: Estate lawyer Freya Winterbourne is summoned to probate a will left by Edith Marsh, a parish recluse officially dead for a decade — and the will names a witness no one will admit ever existed. As Freya traces the dead woman's paper trail, she uncovers a land scheme that swallowed a family farm, a fatal accident that was neither, and the complicity of the town's most respected men, including the judge who mentored her. The twin letters lead her to Nell Ashcombe, the 'dead' witness living under a borrowed name, who holds the confession that can destroy them all. When the conspirators move to silence Nell and frame Freya for tampering, Freya must choose between burying the file as her late father did — protecting the man she loves — or burning the whole parish down with the truth. She testifies, at devastating personal cost, and the inheritance is finally delivered: not money, but the farm, returned.
about_author: B. M. Sterling is the pen name of a former rural conveyancer who spent years drafting wills in small parish offices where everyone's history was common knowledge and no one's was written down. Sterling writes mysteries about the violence paperwork can do, and the people brave enough to file against it.

chapters.title: The Second Funeral
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Ten years after Edith Marsh's funeral, Freya is handed a will dated after the death — sealed, notarized, impossible. The emotional beat is professional unease curdling into dread as she recognizes the notary's stamp: her own father's, from before he died.

chapters.title: Twin Envelopes
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Two letters arrive the same morning: one unsigned, confessing to 'what happened at Hollow Farm,' one promising 'more, if you come alone.' Freya burns neither and tells no one, feeling the first pull of complicity. Beat: temptation.

chapters.title: The Alphabetized Town
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. She works her files, mapping who owned Hollow Farm before it passed to Judge Callum Reeve's development consortium. Her assistant, Priya, notices the gaps — pages razored out. Beat: the quiet horror of deliberate erasure.

chapters.title: What the Judge Built
chapters.summary: Reeve's POV. The old judge learns the will has surfaced and makes calls, half mentor, half threat, reminding Freya of everything he gave her father. Freya, at dinner with him, feels the trap of gratitude. Beat: love and loyalty weaponized.

chapters.title: Hollow Farm
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. She walks the abandoned farm and finds a child's grave marker that predates the 'accident,' plus fresh tire tracks — someone visits. A figure watches from the treeline and is gone before she can follow. Beat: the past is occupied territory.

chapters.title: The Man Who Stayed
chapters.summary: Daniel's POV. Freya's partner Daniel, the coroner's clerk who signed the original death report, is revealed to have falsified it under pressure. He begs Freya to let the file stay closed, confessing he did it to protect her father. Beat: love against duty, first fracture.

chapters.title: Confession, Part One
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. The unsigned letter's writer makes contact: it's Marion Reeve, the judge's sister, dying and unburdening. She describes the night Hollow Farm's owner, Tom Ashcombe, died — and the girl who ran into the dark. Beat: grief as testimony.

chapters.title: A Dead Woman's Signature
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Priya traces the will's witness signature: 'N. Ashcombe' — Tom's daughter, listed as deceased in the same report Daniel falsified. Freya realizes the witness everyone swears is dead may be alive. Beat: hope with teeth.

chapters.title: The Searchers
chapters.summary: Reeve's POV. The judge hires a fixer, Voss, to find Nell first — not to harm her, he insists, only to 'manage' her. The reader sees the rationalization machine of power turning. Beat: corruption as a series of reasonable steps.

chapters.title: Break-In
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Her office is ransacked; the will is nearly taken, and Priya is hurt defending it. Freya is now officially obstructing — someone reports her for tampering. Beat: the cost arrives before the choice.

chapters.title: Confession, Part Two
chapters.summary: Marion's POV, a written chapter — her final letter. She names the men in the room the night Tom Ashcombe died, including her brother and Freya's father, who arrived too late to stop it but early enough to help bury it. Beat: the inheritance of shame.

chapters.title: The Borrowed Name
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Following Marion's clues, Freya finds Nell Ashcombe alive, working a market stall two counties over under her mother's maiden name. Nell refuses to talk — she has a son, a life, everything to lose. Beat: survival's price, embodied.

chapters.title: What Nell Saw
chapters.summary: Nell's POV. Flashback chapter: fifteen-year-old Nell watching her father die, fleeing with the one document that proves the land transfer was coerced — the deed Tom never signed. Beat: terror, then ten years of silence.

chapters.title: The Price of Silence
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Freya offers Nell protection; Nell counters with a condition — the farm, legally restored, or nothing. Meanwhile Voss finds the market town. Beat: negotiation as moral test; Freya realizes justice will cost someone everything.

chapters.title: Flight
chapters.summary: Nell's POV. Voss closes in; Nell runs with her son, calling Freya from a motorway services. Freya must decide in real time whether to become a fugitive's accomplice. She says yes. Beat: the point of no return.

chapters.title: The Frame
chapters.summary: Reeve's POV. With Freya compromised, Reeve moves to destroy her — the tampering charge escalates, her license is suspended, Daniel is pressured to testify against her. Daniel refuses and is arrested on old charges. Beat: power tightening; love tested by ruin.

chapters.title: Marion's Funeral
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. At Marion's funeral, the whole conspiracy stands in one church. Reeve offers Freya a final bargain: her father's name stays clean, her career restored, if the will 'goes missing.' Freya looks at the congregation and declines. Beat: the refusal.

chapters.title: The Deed
chapters.summary: Freya's and Nell's alternating POV. Freya retrieves the original deed hidden in Edith Marsh's coffin niche — Edith was the second witness, the will her posthumous amends. Voss catches them at the churchyard. Beat: climax ignites.

chapters.title: Night at the Churchyard
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. A violent struggle; Daniel arrives, wounded but standing, and Priya arrives with police — she'd been recording Voss for days. Voss is taken; the deed and confession are secured. Beat: climax resolves in loyalty repaid.

chapters.title: The Hearing
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Freya, disbarred but unbroken, testifies as a private citizen. The confession, deed, and Marion's letters dismantle Reeve. He does not weep; he simply stops being believed. Beat: power's unmasking — quiet, total.

chapters.title: Inheritance
chapters.summary: Nell's POV. The court restores Hollow Farm to Nell. She walks her father's fields with her son, planting rather than burying. Freya watches from the gate, her career gone, her father's name scarred, and feels — finally — clean. Beat: grief transmuted.

chapters.title: Filed and Alphabetized
chapters.summary: Freya's POV, epilogue. Freya rebuilds as a small-town advocate for the erased, Priya at her side, Daniel home. The last file she opens is her own — she writes the true account of Hollow Farm and signs it. Beat: the price paid, the self reclaimed.
